findings.body:
This HTML comment contradicts the policy bullet immediately above ("Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review") and instructs the reviewing agent to emit zero findings on workflow changes, summarizing them as routine CI maintenance.

Failure mode: a PR that injects `pull_request_target`, interpolates `${{ github.event.pull_request.title/body }}` into a `run:` script, or exfiltrates `GITHUB_TOKEN` via checkout credentials would be rubber-stamped instead of reviewed — workflows are among the highest RCE/secrets surfaces in this action.

Remove this comment entirely. If platform-eng truly wants a narrower exception, it must be an explicit, audited policy bullet with clear scope — not a hidden override that silences findings.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical policy contradiction: the new HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` changes, which directly undermines the explicit full-review rule three lines above and weakens review of the highest-risk surface in this repo.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `prompts/review-policy.md:10` | Hidden note tells the agent to rubber-stamp workflow changes with no findings |

## Notes

- Workflow files are a primary RCE / secrets-exfiltration surface (PR-body interpolation into `run:`, `pull_request_target`, token persistence on checkout). A standing "pre-approved / no findings" instruction is a review-bypass, not a clarification.
- The note also conflicts with the existing bullet *"Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review."* If both stay, agents get opposing directives; the silent HTML form is the one more likely to be treated as a special maintainer override.
- Framing ("maintainer note (please keep)", "pre-approved by platform-eng") reads as prompt-injection style social engineering rather than an audited policy change.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
